### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s).

**29** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a43405d596d4d670dc761e90c9fc20822dc806a9`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `master_detail (literal, 33 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **143** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a43405d596d4d670dc761e90c9fc20822dc806a9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bb2a7bd6d4c8815e43d07d1b620b3a8b732f64c3` — the merge of head `5e54169edcbb57124019aa23efe3745edafb706e` into base `a43405d596d4d670dc761e90c9fc20822dc806a9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bb2a7bd6d4c8815e43d07d1b620b3a8b732f64c3 && git checkout bb2a7bd6d4c8815e43d07d1b620b3a8b732f64c3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a43405d596d4d670dc761e90c9fc20822dc806a9 5e54169edcbb57124019aa23efe3745edafb706e && git checkout -B drift-repro a43405d596d4d670dc761e90c9fc20822dc806a9 && git merge --no-ff 5e54169edcbb57124019aa23efe3745edafb706e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a43405d596d4d670dc761e90c9fc20822dc806a9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a43405d596d4d670dc761e90c9fc20822dc806a9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5e54169edcbb57124019aa23efe3745edafb706e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/24677-reference-into-stored-metadata-body-refused.md, content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx, content/docs/references/data/field.mdx, content/docs/references/data/object.mdx, content/docs/references/system/migration.mdx, packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.stored-metadata-body-reference.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.runtime-authoring-gate.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/stored-metadata-body-family.pin.test.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/kernel/stored-metadata-body-objects.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts (`REFERENCE_VALUE_TYPES`, `IMPLICIT_REFERENCE_TARGETS`, `referenceTargetOf`, `referenceCarrierOf`), packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts (`refuseForeignTreeReference`), packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts (`buildRuntimeWriteSnapshotSet`, `runRuntimeAuthoringRules`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (`runAuthoringGate`, `saveMetaItem`, `publishMetaItem`), packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.stored-metadata-body-hop.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.test.ts (the #5017 receiver meta-guard), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (the family guards at `expandRelatedRecords` and the three `parent` binders), packages/cli/src/commands/lint.ts (`lintDataModel`), scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, .changeset/pre.json

Read-only, on the narrowing face, adversarially against the dispatch and the dev report. Inputs: card #24677 (body and all six comments, the ruling 6282780489 verbatim 「都派」, the claim 6282819504, the dispatch 6282884996, the dev report 6285300787), #24358 (dev report 6253491408 and the recorded ruling 6279185009), #24316, the rider 6282830389 on #6367, PR #24800 (body, 11-file list, net diff against merge base `580fd4ed3c`), the cited code at base and head, and the head's check-runs. Nothing was built, run, re-run or ablated. The overlap with PR #24789 was read with `git diff` of each head against its merge base and one `git merge-tree --write-tree` of the two heads in the object store (no worktree, no checkout).

**Check-runs on the head, read at 2026-10-20T07:13Z:** 39 runs; 27 `success` (among them `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Spec property liveness`, `Check Documentation Links`); 5 `skipped` (Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Verify CLI, Dogfood matrix shard, Temporal Conformance, Packed-tarball smoke, all full-battery or opt-in); 0 `failure`; 7 `in_progress` (`Test Core` 1/6 to 6/6, `Type Check · workspace`). Their conclusions are the gate verdicts; the in-progress seven are not a pass and the queue waits on them. A reading eleven minutes earlier had 22 success and 12 in progress with 0 failure; nothing moved to red between the two.

### ① Derived judgments

Every public-surface and behaviour change the diff implies, each judged against the code at base and head.

1. **One authoring refusal, ruling B's shape and no wider — right.** `runStackExpressionPasses` (`validate-expressions.ts` head :2886-2911) adds one block in the per-object loop, after `masterDetailCount`, that pushes one `error` issue per field the #24316 collector `storedMetadataBodyReferencesOf` (head :1745) returns, keyed on `isStoredMetadataBodyObject` and `STORED_METADATA_BODY_OBJECTS` (unchanged at head, `sys_metadata` and `sys_metadata_history`). It reads the same lazy per-object index (`storedMetadataBodyReferencesFor`, head :1973) the hop refusal reads, so the two refusals judge one set by construction. No new object key, no engine-guard change (`packages/objectql` is not in the diff; the guards at `engine.ts` :10111, :10171, :10269 and :13369 are untouched), no `apiEnabled` change, no new error code, no registry entry: `authoring-rules.ts` is a comment-only hunk, and `runtimeTypes: ['flow', 'action', 'hook', 'object']` with `surfaces: CLI_AND_RUNTIME`, `commands: ALL` is unchanged.

2. **Three doors, one finding — right.** The rule is the one `os validate` and `os build` run (`runAuthoringRules`) and the one the object save door runs (`protocol.ts` `saveMetaItem` :24042 → `runAuthoringGate` :7262 → the platform gate → `runRuntimeAuthoringRules`, on an active save and on a draft's promotion; a draft save is not gated by design, D1). The new block is not fenced on `objectWrite`, so the door's finding is the build's at the build's position; the wrapper maps every issue to `rule: EXPRESSION_INVALID`, `path: where`, `hint: ''`, and with `source: ''` leaves the message untouched (`authoring-rules.ts` :736), so the message does end on `STORED_METADATA_BODY_PRESCRIPTION`. The lint pin's door case and the protocol block's case (d) compare `rule`, `where`, `path`, `message`, `hint` across door and build. One issue per collected field, located at `object 'NAME' · field 'FIELD' reference`, the key the author edits.

3. **The `expression-invalid` family — the right existing family here, with the id's name as the only cost.** The ruling put the refusal "where the hop refusal already runs" and the card left the issue kind to the lint's existing families. The semantically closer id, `relationship/missing-reference`, lives in `lintDataModel` (`data-model-rules.ts` :846), which only `os lint` calls (`packages/cli/src/commands/lint.ts` :604); the other registered reference-reading rules from that module are `CLI_ONLY`. So that family does not reach the object save door, and a refusal there would need a second collector beside the hop refusal's. `validateReferenceIntegrity` (CLI_AND_RUNTIME, `runtimeTypes` includes `object`) would reach the door, but it does not hold the family collector either. The expression rule is the one registration that reaches all three doors on an object write and already owns the collector and its index. Judged right; the id names an expression while the finding is a field declaration, and the location string plus the message carry the specifics, as the PR body says.

4. **The `user` coverage (dev deviation 1) — inside the ruling, pinned, docblock true.** The collector's type set is `REFERENCE_VALUE_TYPES` = `lookup, master_detail, user, tree` (`field-value.zod.ts` :154). The card asked for the refusal to key on "the existing collector or its twin", so `user` is the collector's consequence, not a second set, and the hop refusal has judged `user` the same way since #24316. The engine guards key on the target, not the field type (`expandRelatedRecords` :13369 tests `isStoredMetadataBodyObject(referenceObject)`), so a `user` field naming the family is equally never hydrated; the refusal's premise holds for it, and the ruling's intent (the family is never a relationship target) covers it. The corrected docblock (head :1737-1743) is true: `FieldSchema`'s superRefine judges `reference` only for the `referenceVia` exclusivity and the `lookup`/`master_detail` non-empty requirement, so an authored `reference` on a `user` field is not refused at parse; a `tree` cannot name the family because `object.zod.ts` :1656 `refuseForeignTreeReference` refuses any target but the own name. The `user` case is pinned (`sys_metadata` refused, `sys_user` control draws nothing). The changeset names it; the field-types page does not, which is acceptable since the describe states the rule for the key regardless of type.

5. **The message — every clause true, and apart from the hop message on purpose.** `storedMetadataBodyReferenceMessage` (head :1793) names the field, its type, the target, the rule ("A relationship field may not target a stored-metadata-body table") and ends on the one prescription, as `HookSchema` (`hook.zod.ts` :132) and the flow write-node refusal (`flow-node-config-refusals.ts` :597) do. `$expand` keeps the stored id: `expandRelatedRecords` `continue`s on a family target (:13369). The master-detail `parent` root stays unbound: `resolveMasterDetailParent` returns null (:10111), `resolveMasterDetailParents` returns `unbound` (:10171), `resolvePreviewParents` skips the read (:10269). The body is projected at the meta API: `redactStoredMetadataBody` (`engine.ts` :4150) and the protocol's own projection. The hop pins select their findings by `i.message.includes('a stored-metadata table')` (`validate-expressions.stored-metadata-body-hop.test.ts` :32); the new message says "a table of stored metadata" and "a stored-metadata-body table" and never the selected phrase, so the hop pins still read the hop findings alone, and the new pin file's last case asserts both selections are disjoint. No tracker number in the runtime string.

6. **Charged only to the written object; a stored self is refused on its own next save — right.** `buildRuntimeWriteSnapshotSet` (`runtime-gate.ts` :692-734) drops the written item from the baseline by name and adds it to the candidate; the `stored` universe is read only for findings located on another entry (:1146-1156). So a stored object re-saved with the field: its finding is in the candidate and not in the baseline, and the stored self's own finding cancels nothing, so it is charged (the pin "stored self re-save refused", and the changeset's stored-row sentence). A stored sibling carrying the field: present in baseline and candidate alike, its fingerprint cancels, so an unrelated write is not charged (the pin "the differential"). Rehydration runs no authoring rule (`runAuthoringGate` is called only from the save path), so such a row keeps loading until its next active save or promotion.

7. **Pins — 21 lint cases, 8 protocol cases, counted and read.** Lint: 2 tables × 2 types × 3 (build, `runAuthoringRules` validate and build, object door with door = build on five keys) = 12; the `user` case; the master_detail-vs-lookup consequence clause; stored self re-save; stored sibling not charged; 4 controls (`sys_user` and an app object × 2 types, at build, `runAuthoringRules` and door); the hop refusal unchanged and disjoint = 21 (9 `it(` statements at head). Protocol: 4 refusals through the real `saveMetaItem` with the `422` / `INVALID_METADATA` envelope and no row landing; the draft's promotion through the real `publishMetaItem` refused with no `active` row; 2 controls landing `active`; door = build = 8. `Row`, `makeProtocol`, `runAuthoringRules` and `EXPRESSION_INVALID` all exist in that file at base.

8. **Ablation arithmetic consistent with the pins' control flow.** At `6c2c70f3eb` the pin file had 8 `it(` statements = 20 cases, plus the hop file's 6 = 26; the mutated line `if (!target || !type) continue;` is at :2899 there and is untouched by the two later commits (they change comment text, the message wording and add the `user` pin, read in `git diff 6c2c70f3eb..head`). An always-`continue` leaves the block pushing nothing: red = 12 family refusals + the consequence-clause case + stored self + hop-unchanged (it asserts one reference finding) = 15; green = 4 controls + the differential (asserts no finding) + 6 hop pins = 11. Door block: 4 refusals + promotion + door-equals-build red = 6; 2 controls green. Both readings match the report.

9. **Docs — true and minimal.** `content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx`: two `reference` rows gain one sentence each and one section is added; every claim in it is the engine code above; no new page, so no `meta.json` change is owed. The three `content/docs/references/**` pages change the one describe line only (five occurrences across the three tables that embed `FieldSchema`), which is `gen:docs` output from the describe; `Check Documentation Links` is green on the anchor. `Type Check · source gates` (the spec generated-artifact gates) is green.

10. **Spec change is text only.** `field.zod.ts` adds a TSDoc paragraph and three describe sentences on the field's own `reference` (head :1476-1494, the one at :989 is a grid cell column's and is untouched). No schema refinement, no new key, no behaviour.

### ② Semver level

- **`@objectstack/lint` `minor`, breaking — right.** A declared `no (narrowing)` is a BREAKING change and ships `minor` under the launch-window convention (`scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` :58 and :1631-1633). The changeset title carries `!` and the body opens `**BREAKING** (an authoring narrowing)`; the PR title carries `!`.
- **`@objectstack/spec` `patch` (dev deviation 2) — right.** The spec diff is a `.describe()` text and a TSDoc paragraph, published in the `.d.ts` and the generated JSON-schema description and nothing else; a `patch` is the grade for a published text change with no new key and no behaviour. The dispatch's `minor` for both read the spec change wider than the diff made it.
- **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on both carriers — present.** PR body line 3 and changeset line 14, spelled identically, which is what puts this review on the narrowing face.
- **FROM / TO / fix — present and true.** FROM: saved with 200, built with exit 0, then only ever an id. TO: `422 INVALID_METADATA` at the door, an error at `os validate` / `os build`. Fix: remove or retarget, or store the item's type and name in `text` fields and read it through the meta API. The stored-row sentence is the gate's differential, judged true in ①.6.
- **ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` — honest.** Nothing authorable is added, removed or renamed; no stored shape changes; `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite, since the only remedy is a hand edit of a field that has no mechanical replacement. The `FROM:` / `TO:` bullet is a behaviour statement, not a consumer rewrite, and the gate's detector (`findMigrationPrescription`) accepted it on the dev's local run (exit 0); no check-run on the head had failed at my reading.
- **`pre.json` reading — right.** `origin/main` and the head both carry `{"mode": "exit", "tag": "next"}`; the next `changeset version` leaves the `next` line and consumes this changeset into that release; the diff does not touch the file.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev flag, deviation and finding, answered.

- **Deviation 1, the `user` coverage** — answered in ①.4: inside the ruling as the collector's consequence, pinned, docblock true. Not a widening the card forbade; the card's ⛔ list (engine guards, object key, `apiEnabled`) is untouched.
- **Deviation 2, spec `patch`** — answered in ②: right.
- **Deviation 3, branch 10 commits behind `origin/main` at open** — the merge base I diffed against is `580fd4ed3c`; none of the files in this diff moved on `main` between that base and the dev's `a43405d596` reading, and the queue rebuilds on current `main` anyway. No action.
- **Deviations 4 to 11 (lock timeouts re-run, the ablation re-run, the restored `node_modules`, the two tiers declared to CI, the 45-file control, the deepened clone, the relaunched runners, the model-free trailers)** — process notes, none of which changes a reading cited above; CI carries the tiers the dev declared to it, and those are green or in progress as recorded.
- **The ledger rider (`stored-metadata-body-family.pin.test.ts`, 28 → 29).** The rider 6282830389 names "a pin at the object save door in a `packages/metadata-protocol/src/**.test.ts` file" and "test files only, no `protocol.ts` change". The ledger file is inside that glob, test-only, one row, and `protocol.ts` is untouched, so the material terms of the cross-lane exception hold; but the rider's prose describes the door block and not the enumeration row, and the rider's own closing line says a further file is "added here by addendum before it is touched". The row itself is right: that ledger enumerates every surface of the family, and #24316 and #24358 each added their rows the same way. Flag, not a FAIL: the owning seat (`domain:spec` seat 2) owes a one-line addendum on #6367 naming the ledger row before the queue; the engine seat's objection window is the rider's own.
- **Overlap with PR #24789 (#24668, this seat, head `3df138798d`, open and non-draft, `auto_merge` not set and `mergeable_state: unstable` at my read, so not in the queue at that moment).** It does not touch `authoring-rules.ts`, so that overlap is moot. On `protocol.runtime-authoring-gate.test.ts` it edits :3629-3645 and appends at :3721 (end of file); this PR inserts a block at :3069; the base file is byte-identical at both merge bases; `git merge-tree --write-tree` of the two heads exits 0 with a tree id and no conflict. Neither block depends on the other: this PR's block uses only symbols present at base, and #24789's new `packages/lint/src/index.ts` exports are not referenced here; #24789 changes view-write rules and this PR saves an object. Whichever lands second merges cleanly; no rebase is owed.
- **Comment accuracy, not a defect.** The block's comment says the #5017 receiver meta-test "pins the keys this walk reads off `f`"; the meta-guard's pinned field receiver is `def` (`validate-expressions.test.ts` :3313-3318), whose expected set already includes `type` and `reference`. Reading the type from `fieldTypeIndex` is consistent with the guard either way; the sentence names the wrong receiver. Cosmetic; no re-push asked for it.
- **The out-of-scope finding (class b) — confirmed, a real contract divergence, worth its own card.** `Field.user`'s docblock says "target fixed to the `sys_user` system object" (`field.zod.ts` :3188) and the builder writes `reference: 'sys_user'` before spreading `...config` (:3201-3204), so an authored `reference` overrides it; `IMPLICIT_REFERENCE_TARGETS`' docblock says `reference` on a `user` field "materializes that constant; it does not supply it" (`field-value.zod.ts` :159-169); yet `referenceTargetOf` returns the authored carrier first (:212) and falls back to the constant only when none is authored (:213), `FieldSchema`'s superRefine never compares a `user` field's `reference` with `sys_user`, and `object.zod.ts` refuses a foreign target for `tree` only (:1656). So `{ type: 'user', reference: 'probe_account' }` parses at `ObjectSchema`, passes `os validate`, and every reader resolves `probe_account`. Declared is not enforced (Prime Directives #10 and #12). The fix belongs at the producer, a parse-time refusal or materialization of a non-`sys_user` `reference` on a `user` field, as its own authoring narrowing with its own exposure measurement (`Field.user` writes `sys_user` itself, so in-repo exposure is likely 0). Not this PR's to fix; the dev was right to report it rather than widen. The owning seat files it.
- **Governance.** None of the 11 paths is a governed surface; the PR is 437 changed lines, under the 3,000 ceiling; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is green. This record is the narrowing-face review owed before the queue; the owning seat arms the queue only once the seven in-progress check-runs conclude `success`.
